ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows one large rectangle divided into seven congruent smaller rectangles. The top strip contains three congruent rectangles oriented vertically side by side. The lower part contains four congruent rectangles oriented horizontally, arranged as two columns and two rows. Reasoning: Let each small rectangle have short side x and long side y. From the top strip, the large rectangle's width is 3x. From the lower two-column arrangement, the same large width is 2y. Therefore 3x = 2y, so y = 3x/2. The height of the large rectangle is the height of the top vertical rectangles plus the two lower horizontal rows, which is y + 2x. The perimeter is 65, so 2[(3x) + (y + 2x)] = 65. Substitute y = 3x/2: 2[5x + 3x/2] = 65, so 2[13x/2] = 65, hence 13x = 65 and x = 5. Then y = 15/2. The large rectangle has width 3x = 15 and height y + 2x = 15/2 + 10 = 35/2. Its area is 15 · 35/2 = 525/2.

Use the text statement that the large rectangle has perimeter 65: 2[(3x) + (y + 2x)] = 65. Combine with y = 3x/2 to solve x = 5 and y = 15/2. Then compute large rectangle area as width times height: (3x)(y + 2x) = 15 · 35/2 = 525/2.
